newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Superphenix reactor to increase power.
newsitem.headline: France's Superphenix reactor to increase power.

text.p: French nuclear safety regulators said on Tuesday they had agreed to allow the trouble-plagued Superphenix fast-breeder nuclear reactor to run at up to 90 percent of its 1,200-megawatt capacity.

The reactor, which has been operating at up to 60 percent of full power since February, has been dogged by expensive faults. It was restarted last December after being shut down due a steam leak in a generator.

The plant was turned into a research laboratory last year, to study recycling nuclear waste, well short of its original design as a fast-breeder producing more plutonium than it burns while generating electricity.
The Superphenix was singled out as a waste of state money earlier this month by France's public spending watchdog, the Court of Accounts.

The watchdog said the state had spent 60 billion francs ($11.53 billion) on the reactor at Creys-Malville near the Swiss border, although it has operated for only a dozen months since it was commissioned 20 years ago.
The Environment Ministry's Nuclear Safety Authority said it was due to be shut down next January for restructuring work.
